THE CHARRED ONE TAKES A DEEP BREATH ...
THE HEART OF THE CHARRED ONE
This statue shows the Hero of Sugar.
This statue shows the very first cookie ever baked.

Take flour and sugar, fine and light,
add butter soft, just measured right.
Crack in an egg, be quick and neat,
so all your cookies turn out sweet.

Now stir the dough and knead it slow,
until it makes your spirits glow.
Shape little circles, one by one,
with chocolate chips for extra fun.

Into the oven, one-eighty degrees,
ten minutes later, smell that breeze!
Then let them rest, then help yourself —
fresh cookies, straight from the shelf!

When the oven glows and the journey starts,
when the scent of chocolate warms our hearts,
then you know for sure the time is here:
the cookies are ready, give a cheer!

Crumbs ahead, we never give in,
through sugar storms and flames we'll win!
Together strong, whatever we face,
every cookie believes in its dreams and wins the race!

Chocolate, vanilla, big or small,
no cookie's ever alone at all.
And when the donuts block our way,
we'll march on together, come what may!

Crumbs ahead!
The future's in our hand!
Crumbs ahead!
For all of Sugarland!

In the Year of the Great Sugar, a bitter war broke out between the cookies and the donuts.

The cookies, hard and proud, marched under the banner of chocolate. But the donuts, round and glazed, defended their sweet throne with all their might.
For three days and three nights the land of bakeries trembled. Crumbs covered the ground, and icing drifted like snow across the fields.
But when the battle would not end, a single cookie stepped forward. Bravely it stood between the two armies and convinced cookies and donuts alike to lay down their weapons.
And so the Great Cookie War came to an end. But that brave cookie is celebrated to this very day as the Hero of Sugar.

Every weapon reacts differently to your buffs. Under WEAPONS, BUFFS and EVOS each entry says what Extra Shot, Area (AOE), Duration and Cooldown do for it.

Damage, crit chance and crit damage always work on every hit of every weapon.

The values come from level-up buffs, the skill tree and the mixer. They all add up.

Extra Shot gives weapons more projectiles per attack.

Fractions count as a chance: with 1.5 extra shots every attack gets one guaranteed extra shot and a 50% chance of a second. With 0.6 it is a 60% chance of one. It is rolled again on every attack.

The Extra Shot buff counts 1:1 on every weapon. Extra shots from the skill tree and mixer follow the weapon's ratio instead: at 1:3 a weapon needs three of them for one more projectile. With 2 it has a 67% chance of one more, with 3 it gets one for sure.

Things that stay around, like wisps or kunai in the ring, only count whole extra shots. Otherwise their number would keep jumping.

Some weapons ignore Extra Shot completely, for example when more projectiles in the same spot would just be more damage.

Area makes everything bigger that hits a zone: explosions, puddles, rings, slashes and on some weapons the projectiles themselves.

It is the radius that grows. +50% radius means more than double the area (x2.25), so area weapons gain the most.

Weapons that only hit single targets get nothing from it.

Duration extends everything that stays on the ground or keeps working: puddles, pools, saws, vortexes, turrets, crumbs, burns and slows.

If something lasts longer than the weapon needs for its next attack, several are down at once. Then Duration works like more damage.

Weapons that hit instantly get nothing from it.

Cooldown is the pause between two attacks of a weapon. Less cooldown works on all weapons.

Everything together goes down to 35% of the base value at most.

Weapons with a duration overlap more attacks because of it.

Damage increases every hit of every weapon.

Crit chance is the chance for a hit to be critical. Crit damage sets how much more a critical hit deals.

Many small hits roll for crits more often, big hits get more out of crit damage.

Endless mode is waiting for you.
Every character is a different food and plays differently. *Click* a portrait to take a look. *CHOOSE* (or Enter) takes them along on your next run.
Every character brings their own *starting weapon* and has their own *skill tree* and their own builds at the *workbench*. What you learn with one stays with them.
Grey characters are still *locked*. You get them through *achievements* - the capsule tells you which ones under UNLOCKS.

Every character has their own skill tree with four paths: *Combat*, *Spirit*, *Knowledge* and *Luck*. Pick the path on the left, the nodes next to it. A node can only be learned once the one before it is learned.
All the XP you collect in a run also goes to your character's account. Every *character level* gives you a *skill point*. Click a node and press *LEARN*.
The first time a character beats a boss, they get a *bonus level*. *RESET* gives you all your points back.
You don't have to level every character on their own: while you play with one, *all the others passively earn a little XP* too. When you switch, a few skill points are often already waiting for you.
The character you are playing right now always levels up the fastest, though.
At the workbench you decide *what* your level-ups are drawn from. Nothing is equipped yet - it's the *pot* for your level-up cards. Whatever isn't in it won't show up in the run.
*Click* a tile in the *library* on the right to put it into the pool. Click it in the pool and it's taken out again. Slot 1 always belongs to your character's starting weapon.
Every slot in a run opens *3 places* - buy more slots in the shop. Whatever you leave empty is filled *at random* when the run starts.
Two matching ingredients at *max level* fuse into an *evolution* during the run. The bar at the bottom shows which evos your build can reach - *all* opens the full list.
Click an *evo* at the bottom: the workbench puts the matching weapons and buffs into the pool *by itself* - as long as there is enough room left.
*1* to *4* switch between saved builds - the last one you picked goes into the run. *RANDOM* rolls a build for you, *CLEAR* empties it.
You can buy more build slots in the *shop*.
Pick a *stop* on the route and choose whether you want to play *STORY* or *ENDLESS*. The run only starts with *PLAY* (or Enter).
The profile on the right shows the world's boss, its enemy types and your best time.

*Story*: survive until the boss shows up and defeat it - that opens the *next world*. *Endless*: once you've beaten all five worlds and destroyed the Charred One's heart, you can play every world without end, for as long as you last.
You get gold after *every* run - even when you lose.
Every station has *three stars* below it. Beat a world in Story and you get stars by difficulty: *Normal* one, *Hard* two, *Very Hard* all three.
Beat a world on *Very Hard* on your very first try and all three stars light up at once. You set the difficulty at the *chili shelf* in Rico's shop.
How spicy do you like it?
At the *chili shelf* you pick the difficulty. *Normal* is a little easier, *Hard* is the game as it was meant to be played, and *Very Hard* is much harder - enemies can take more and hit harder.
You can switch *any time* in the hub. Your choice applies from the next run.
Every Story win earns stars in the *level select*: *Normal* one, *Hard* two, *Very Hard* all three. Stars you have earned stay.
A win on *Very Hard* gives *all three* stars right away - even the first time.
This is where you spend the gold from your runs. *UPGRADES* are permanent improvements - more slots, rerolls, starting XP and more. Under *UNLOCKS* you buy new weapons and buffs.
Changed your mind? *RESET* refunds the gold for all purchases so you can spend it again.
The capsule holds your *achievements* and what they *unlock* - new characters, worlds and shop items. Select an entry to see how to get it.
Learn the *bestiary* in the skill tree and the capsule counts every enemy type. The more of one type you defeat, the more damage you deal to it.
